title: Exact Finite-Channel Schur Moments of the Wigner-Smith Matrix with a Tunnel Barrier
abstract: We consider the Wigner--Smith time-delay matrix of a chaotic cavity with broken time-reversal symmetry, a finite number $M$ of equivalent open channels, and a uniform tunnel barrier of reflection probability $R$. Exact random-matrix results for nonideal coupling are known at the level of the joint matrix distribution, whereas explicit finite-channel formulas for Schur moments are much less developed. We show that every Schur moment of the nonideal Wigner--Smith matrix factorizes into its ideal-coupling inverse-Laguerre value and a barrier factor given by a circular unitary ensemble (CUE) average of a Schur polynomial. A dual-Cauchy generating function reduces the latter to a Toeplitz determinant with a rational symbol, placing the barrier problem within the classical theory of exact CUE characteristic-polynomial ratios.   For one-row partitions, specializing the exact CUE ratio formula gives a closed generating function for all barrier coefficients and therefore all finite delay-time moments in the allowed range $n\le M$. The exact ratio formula decomposes into a sector visible to the semiclassical expansion and an additional contribution proportional to $R^{M+1}$, which is invisible to every algebraic order in $1/M$. For the second moment, this contribution exactly reproduces the exponentially small term in the known random-matrix expression for $\langleτ_W^2\rangle$ that is absent from the semiclassical expansion. We also derive an exact finite sum for all one-column partitions and an exact complement symmetry for Schur averages inside the $M\times M$ square. The new contribution therefore lies not in the underlying CUE ratio identities, which are classical, but in combining them with the exact nonideal Wigner--Smith mapping and extracting the resulting finite-channel time-delay formulas and corrections to semiclassical Schur-moment conjectures.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the exact finite-channel Schur moments for the Wigner-Smith time-delay matrix in a chaotic cavity with a tunnel barrier. By mapping the problem onto known CUE determinant identities, the authors derive closed-form generating functions that reveal finite-size corrections to standard semiclassical predictions. This provides a highly precise tool for analyzing quantum transport in mesoscopic systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive exact, finite-channel formulas for the Schur moments of the Wigner-Smith time-delay matrix when the coupling between a chaotic cavity and the outside world is nonideal due to a tunnel barrier.
main_result: The Schur moments are shown to factorize into a known ideal-coupling value and a universal Circular Unitary Ensemble (CUE) barrier factor, leading to closed generating functions for all finite delay-time moments up to the channel number M.
method: The methodology combines Random Matrix Theory (RMT) techniques, specifically using symmetric function methods and determinant-generating functions, to reduce the problem to calculating Toeplitz determinants derived from CUE averages.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a chaotic cavity with broken time-reversal symmetry coupled to $M$ open channels via a uniform tunnel barrier characterized by a reflection probability $R$. The physics is encoded in the Wigner-Smith time-delay matrix.
key_observables: Schur moments of the Wigner-Smith matrix, $\langle s_\lambda(Q_R) angle$, and the Wigner time delay $	au_W$.
important_parameters: The number of open channels ($M$), the reflection probability ($R$), and the partition index ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the unitary symmetry class ($ eta=2$), the existence of a uniform tunnel barrier, and relies on established exact formulas for CUE characteristic-polynomial ratios.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the factorization of the nonideal Schur moment into an ideal-coupling part and a CUE barrier factor. It then uses dual-Cauchy generating functions to represent the barrier factor as a Toeplitz determinant. Finally, it derives closed-form generating functions for one-row and one-column partitions, explicitly revealing finite-channel corrections beyond semiclassical approximations.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, exact finite-size corrections to semiclassical predictions in quantum chaos, which is crucial for understanding transport properties in mesoscopic systems where finite coupling effects dominate.
